LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 15.3.1 AFFIRMATIVE AND NEGATIVE SENTENCES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.3: Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences, part of Strand 15 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do we use affirmative statements? 2. Why is it important to use the right sentence when saying something?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. differentiate between affirmative and negative sentences in spoken and written contexts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. construct affirmative and negative sentences in varied contexts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the expressive role of sentences in effective communication. ● In pairs, learners are guided to search online and offline for the differences between affirmative and negative sentences and share them with peers. ● In groups, learners are guided to role-play a dialogue with affirmative and negative sentences and record themselves. ● In groups, learners are guided to watch or listen to a conversation (supported with sign language interpretatio

   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: using critical inquiry as learners make affirmative and negative sentences on the tourist attraction sites in Kenya

● Digital literacy is developed as learners search online and offline for the differences between affirmative and negative sentences and

share them with peers.

Values:
● Unity is enhanced as learners share sentences made in the form of charts for peer review

● Patriotism is enhanced as learners read texts on tourist attraction sites.

Link to other subjects:

● The learner relates the concept of affirmative and negative constructions to their learning in Kiswahili or Kenya Sign Language
